title: Capacity booking lifecycle: entitlement checks, canary scaling policies, and supply reconciliation
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Purpose: define an operationally-safe, customer-facing lifecycle for Dedicated capacity bookings that combines entitlement validation, canary autoscale windows, and end-of-cycle supply reconciliation. Scope: intake form changes, entitlement matrix, automated preflight checks, canary scaling policies (burst, sustained, cooldown), billing attribution rules, and a reconciliation runbook for provisioning mismatches. Out of scope for this ticket: billing UI work and legal contract language (handled by Finance/Legal).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form with required fields and validation (product, expected qps/latency percentiles, committed RUs) is published and linked from Console
Automatic entitlement checks run at intake time with deterministic outcomes: approve / needs-review / deny
Canary autoscale policy template defined (min, target, max, burst budget, cooldown) and implemented in autoscale engine spike by ENG
Reconciliation runbook created and verified with a dry-run against last quarter's onboarding data
End-to-end test demonstrating a booking that triggers canary scaling, then a rollback path (quota exceed -> fallback to model-variant) documented
Documentation updated in Confluence and Console help with expected SLA language and lead times

decisions: Canary window semantics: decided on a two-stage canary (fast burst window up to 2x committed RU for 15 minutes, followed by a sustained window up to 1.25x for 6 hours) to balance developer experience and fleet safety.

Entitlement enforcement: system will auto-approve if billing & quota checks pass and the customer is in the 'committed' tier; otherwise route to human reviewer. Avoid strict automated denial to reduce false negatives.
Burst policy vs. strict guarantees: chosen hybrid approach with a small provisioned buffer and explicit SLAs tied to committed throughput; all burst usage is meter-logged and visible in Console.
notes: Open questions: 1) how to expose provisional buffer to customers in billing statements without legal language; 2) operational thresholds for automatic escalation to oncall; 3) whether to include region affinity in intake form or infer from committed usage. Next steps: finalize entitlement matrix, unblock ENG PRs, run 2 dry reconciliation exercises, schedule customer beta for March 17.
